_comment: 3-way cross-binding parity fixtures (issue #1455).
Each fixture names ONE SELECT that is run through all three legs (Python
binding, Node binding, CLI --out json) and canonicalized to the SAME JSON.
`columns` declares the CQL type of every column the query returns. It is
the AUTHORITATIVE input to canonicalization (issue #28: no type guessing
from value shapes), and the harness asserts that the declared column set
equals the set every leg actually returns -- so schema drift reds the test
rather than silently changing what is compared.
`known_divergence` is EMPTY for every fixture and must stay that way. It
exists so a future, deliberately-accepted gap has somewhere to be recorded
with a reason; it is NOT a place to silence a real cross-binding bug. The
issue originally proposed allowlisting `duration` and `time` until #1450
landed -- #1450 IS landed, and all three legs were measured to agree
exactly on both, so nothing is allowlisted.
DECLARED CORPUS GAP: there is NO `varint` column anywhere in the committed
CQL schema corpus (test-data/schemas/**), so the issue's requested
timestamp+blob+varint+decimal fixture is covered for timestamp, blob and
decimal ONLY. The varint canonicalization rule is exercised by
canonical-vectors.json, not by any live fixture. No fixture was fabricated
to close this.
`floor` (issue #1455, B2) is the case floor: an empty or truncated fixture
list would otherwise produce an EMPTY pytest parametrize — one skipped
placeholder and the 3-way comparison silently gone, green. The floor names
the fixtures by NAME, not just a count, so swapping one for a trivial
substitute is caught too.
